title: A parameterized query from a text block

blocks.text: Text blocks make SQL readable, and `formatted()` makes it easy to fill in. The page's warning: `formatted()` has no SQL escaping, so a value typed by a user must never be formatted into a query. Its safe version keeps a `?` placeholder and binds the value later with a `PreparedStatement`.
Write `Sql.select(String table, List<String> columns, String filterColumn)`. It returns these three lines joined by `\n`, with no newline at the end:

items: `<columns>` is the column names joined by `, `, or `*` when the list is empty.
The value to filter by never appears: the query keeps the `?`.

Names are code, not data, so each one is checked: `table`, every column and `filterColumn` must each be **one whole identifier**, a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits or `_` (ASCII only; no `$`, no line break). Anything else throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

cases.says: The query lists the columns, names the table and filters with a ? placeholder, never a value.
A table name that is more than one identifier, such as users; DROP TABLE users, is refused with IllegalArgumentException.
A column name that is not an identifier is refused too.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A user value must never be formatted into SQL; the query keeps a ? placeholder bound by a PreparedStatement.
A text block keeps a SQL query's lines and layout readable.
